entry_sequence.transcript_quote: Continuation scalps, on the other hand, occur around breaks of clean support or resistance.
entry_sequence.action: Wait for price to approach a clean support or resistance level for a continuation break; for long, a break of resistance, or for short, a break of support.
entry_sequence.rationale: The setup is specifically a clean break continuation trade.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: if you are not trading in-play names, you are handicapping yourself.
entry_sequence.action: Only trade the breakout in an in-play stock.
entry_sequence.rationale: The speaker says stock selection is foundational to effective scalping.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: you want to be the first market participant to enter upon the break
entry_sequence.action: Enter as the level breaks; for long, buy just above resistance, or for short, sell just below support.
entry_sequence.rationale: Early execution on the break is the edge in this scalp.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: If buyers continue lifting and the offer size begins to shrink, then suddenly it's gone, you want to be the one buying
entry_sequence.action: Use tape confirmation that the resting liquidity at the level is being consumed before triggering the breakout entry; for long, buyers should lift the offer, or for short, sellers should hit the bid.
entry_sequence.rationale: Real-time order flow confirms whether the level is actually being taken.

stop.transcript_quote: Often, your stop loss would be right below that level if it gets back below the $50.
stop.rationale: The speaker places the stop back below the broken level if the breakout fails.

targets.transcript_quote: potentially kicking it out 10, 20, or even 30 cents higher
targets.rationale: The scalp target is the immediate post-break momentum burst.

confluences.transcript_quote: if you are not trading in-play names, you are handicapping yourself.
confluences.name: in_play_stock
confluences.description: Only take the setup in an in-play stock with strong activity.

confluences.transcript_quote: I want a very well-defined intraday support or resistance level. Ideally, one that aligns on multiple time frames.
confluences.name: clean_multitimeframe_level
confluences.description: The breakout level should be a well-defined intraday support or resistance, ideally aligned across multiple time frames.

confluences.name: elevated_volume
confluences.description: The stock should have unusually high volume for the breakout to matter.

confluences.transcript_quote: The pullbacks are shallow, and each dip finds buyers higher than the previous dip.
confluences.name: tight_consolidation_pressure
confluences.description: Repeated shallow pullbacks and higher dip buyers show pressure building into the breakout level.

confluences.transcript_quote: Your success in a continuation scalp trade will depend heavily on timing and confirmation from real-time order flow.
confluences.name: tape_confirmation
confluences.description: The trade requires real-time order flow confirmation before entry.

confluences.transcript_quote: Are the buyers aggressively lifting into that offer? Are prints going off repeatedly at $50?
confluences.name: aggressive_buyers_or_sellers
confluences.description: For longs, buyers should aggressively lift the offer; for shorts, the mirrored condition is sellers aggressively hitting the bid.

confluences.transcript_quote: If buyers continue lifting and the offer size begins to shrink, then suddenly it's gone
confluences.name: level_getting_taken
confluences.description: The resting liquidity at the level should visibly shrink and disappear, showing the breakout level is being taken.

confluences.transcript_quote: Strong breakouts feel urgent, and you want to see the stock burst through that level with conviction.
confluences.name: urgent_breakout
confluences.description: The breakout should move through the level with urgency and conviction rather than drift.

rejected_strategies.name: continuation_breakout_scalp
rejected_strategies.detail: The speaker also gives fixed-price examples such as buying $10.01/$10.02 or targeting 10 to 30 cents, which are example-specific and not portable fixed-stop/target rules.
